hypotheses.justification: Let A = chartRing κ {t⁻¹}. It is a subalgebra of L, hence a domain. hchartInv says every element of A is aeval t⁻¹ f for some polynomial f. The statement does not mention ht. The proof uses it only through transcendental_inv, to feed eq_span_of_pow_mem and isMaximal_span_tChart_sub. The statement is still true without it, by cases on whether t is transcendental. If t is transcendental, the current proof works. If t is algebraic, then x = t⁻¹ is algebraic (IsAlgebraic.inv_iff). Take a prime 𝔮 containing x. If x ≠ 0, the minimal polynomial p = X·q + C c of x has c ≠ 0. Then c = -x·q(x) lies in 𝔮, because q(x) ∈ A. But c is a unit of κ, so 1 ∈ 𝔮, contradicting primality; this case is vacuous. If x = 0 (t = 0), hchartInv makes every element of A equal to algebraMap κ A (f.coeff 0). So every nonzero element of A is a unit and is not in 𝔮, giving 𝔮 = ⊥ = span {0} = span {t⁻¹}. The degenerate cases t = 0 and trivial κ are covered. hchartInv must stay, since chartRing is an integral closure that can be bigger than κ[t⁻¹]. The proof becomes by_cases ht : Transcendental κ t, with the existing proof in the first branch and the argument above in the second.
